summary: The scientific abstraction and two alternatives are accepted in substance. Repair the incomplete source evidence attached to both model-reuse edges, then regenerate and re-review the digests before image generation.

accepted.finding: Matrix-first paired alignment plus class-text zero-shot transfer is source-bounded and does not claim a new loss primitive.
N by N all-pairs comparison, diagonal paired examples, off-diagonal mismatches, and symmetric image-to-text/text-to-image loss are represented.
Plan correctly distinguishes paper loss from normalized scaled-cosine forward logits returned by released code.
Objective is train-only; reuse edges are control/model-reuse rather than data edges; zero-shot forbids loss, gradients and a new head.
Examples, diagonal marks, and nearest-label output are explicitly schematic with no asserted result.
Matrix bridge and stacked transfer differ materially in spatial/narrative composition while preserving the same source semantics.

required_revisions.observed: Both reuse edges cite only 'At test time the learned text encoder'.
required_revisions.why: That caption fragment supports text-side classifier synthesis, but does not independently support an image-encoder parameter-reuse edge.
required_revisions.required: Use the Section 2.5 whole-model reuse statement 'To apply CLIP to downstream tasks, we reuse this capability' for both reuse edges; optionally retain the Figure 1 caption for text-side synthesis.
required_revisions.constraint: Keep links as inference-phase control/model-reuse only. Do not claim a locally executed frozen checkpoint, requires_grad setting, eval mode, or an inference gradient state.

post_repair_gate: regenerate spec, narrative plan, both briefs, and both prompts through prepare-inputs.mjs
record and consistently propagate the newly emitted semantic and plan digests
preserve train-only objective and zero-shot no-gradient/no-loss/no-new-head restrictions
save raster pixel-only first reading before any source/brief comparison
do not treat raster review as native-artifact acceptance
